s1.syndrome_frame: Facial asymmetry in a neonate with a cerebellopontine angle mass
salient_findings: Enhancing mass in the left cerebellopontine angle and internal auditory canal
Profound hearing loss in the left ear
key_facts: 4-week-old male patient
Left facial asymmetry observed during crying
Passed infant hearing screening
MRI showed an enhancing mass in the left cerebellopontine angle and internal auditory canal
Follow-up MRI showed considerable growth of the mass
ABR testing demonstrated profound hearing loss in the left ear
Histopathological examination revealed a vascular lesion with low levels of mitotic activity
Biphasic lesion composed of vascular nodules among spindle cells
Ki-67 labeling index: 5% to 10%
CD34 and CD31: Positive for endothelial cells

shortlist.label: Hemangioma
shortlist.why_kept: MRI showed an enhancing mass, histopathological examination revealed a vascular lesion

shortlist.label: Lymphangioma
shortlist.why_kept: Histopathological examination showed a biphasic lesion with vascular nodules, similar to lymphangiomatosis

shortlist.label: Lymphangiomatosis
shortlist.why_kept: Histopathological examination revealed a pattern similar to lymphangiomatosis

shortlist.label: Cranial nerve hemangioma
shortlist.why_kept: Mass located in the cerebellopontine angle and internal auditory canal, involving a cranial nerve

shortlist.label: Vestibular schwannoma
shortlist.why_kept: Mass located in the cerebellopontine angle and internal auditory canal, although less likely given the patient's age

raw.rationale: The histopathological examination revealed a vascular lesion with low levels of mitotic activity, biphasic lesion composed of vascular nodules among spindle cells, and positive staining for CD34 and CD31, which are characteristic features of hemangioma.

rejected.label: Lymphangioma
rejected.why: Although the pattern is similar to lymphangiomatosis, the positive staining for CD34 and CD31 suggests a hemangioma rather than a lymphangioma.

rejected.label: Lymphangiomatosis
rejected.why: The presence of a single enhancing mass on MRI and the histopathological features are not consistent with lymphangiomatosis, which typically presents with multiple lesions.

rejected.label: Cranial nerve hemangioma
rejected.why: While the mass is located near the cranial nerve, the histopathological features are more consistent with a hemangioma than a cranial nerve hemangioma.

rejected.label: Vestibular schwannoma
rejected.why: The age of the patient and the histopathological features are not consistent with vestibular schwannoma, which is a rare tumor in infants and typically has a different histological appearance.
